rows.evidence: unchanged since 77c7d7b (git diff checked); round-19 evidence: Re-derived. (1) Q_N = max(Q_(N-1), Z_N) >= Q_(N-1) pointwise, so E[Q_N] >= E[Q_(N-1)]: the expected maximum of the nulls cannot fall as N grows (T). The bound 'at most sqrt(2 ln N)' is Lesson 1 Theorem 2.1 (course/modules/S/S7/L01.html lines 82-84: 'with any joint distribution, and N >= 2. Then E[max Z_n] <= sqrt(2 ln N)'), which the claim cites exactly (cross-lesson theorem, prose-L08-luck-cross-lesson). (2) {Z + delta > Q_N} is contained in {Z + delta > Q_(N-1)} pointwise, so the genuine configuration's win probability cannot rise when a null is added, for any joint law (T). (3) Hence a null's win probability cannot fall (T). The sentence 'Lab 3 below shows what this does to the PBO' points at the Lab 3 block (0.1196 at 2 trials, 0.3375 at 200, the rows of the printed table), which the twin prints (lab-L08-3-twin). Card S7-c227 states claim (1) and card S7-c212 states (2)-(3); both match. rows.evidence: unchanged since 77c7d7b (git diff checked); round-19 evidence: Crossref record: title 'When is the Student $t$-statistic asymptotically standard normal?' (the registry title; the site shows it through plain_title), authors Giné, Götze, Mason, Annals of Probability 25(3) 1514-1531, 1997 (registry matches). Abstract (Crossref, JATS): 'Let X, X_i ... be independent, identically distributed random variables. It is shown that the Student t-statistic based upon the sample ... is asymptotically N(0, 1) if and only if X is in the domain of attraction of the normal law.' Card S7-c236: 'If and only if the returns lie in the domain of attraction of the normal law (Giné, Götze and Mason 1997).' True to the abstract. The card adds 'For iid returns with mean zero (a zero Sharpe ratio)': the zero-mean case is the case in which the Student t-statistic is the test of a zero Sharpe ratio; the abstract's hypothesis on X is iid only (no mean condition is stated), so the restriction is a specialisation, not an extra claim. Grade B with the abstract as locator: accepted as in round 15. Registry note: the theorem number is not reachable from this network (Project Euclid challenge); with it the claim could be graded T (BUILDER_RULES 2.2 would then apply). Freshness: JMVA 2013 10.1016/j.jmva.2012.08.012 extends the result to the multivariate case (a generalisation, not a contest).

def test_a_dry_run_reports_what_the_run_would_do(
    argv: list[str],
    expected: str,
    writes: int,
    unit: str,
    tmp_path: Path,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str],
) -> None:
    # A dry run for a DOI the registry already holds said WOULD ADD, though the run itself updates that entry.
    import add_reference
    from refs import registry

    held = _entry(key="held1995title", doi="10.1/held", url=None, isbn=[], verified_by="crossref")
    saved: list[object] = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(add_reference, "CACHE_DIR", tmp_path)
    monkeypatch.setattr(add_reference, "by_doi", lambda cand, doi: (work(doi=doi), {}, ""))
    monkeypatch.setattr(registry, "load", lambda: [dict(held, source_strings=[])])
    monkeypatch.setattr(registry, "save", saved.append)
    source = ["--source", "Smith (1995), Journal of Finance 50(1)", "--used-by", unit]
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.argv", ["add_reference.py", *argv, *source])
    assert add_reference.main() == 0
    lines = capsys.readouterr().out.splitlines()
    assert len(lines) == 1 and lines[0].startswith(expected)
    assert len(saved) == writes
    if writes:
        # The run stores the union in the entry it saves, not only in its printed line.
        assert saved[0][0]["used_by"] == ["M2", "S7"]  # type: ignore[index]

def test_a_dry_run_reports_what_the_run_would_do(
    argv: list[str],
    expected: str,
    writes: int,
    unit: str,
    tmp_path: Path,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str],
) -> None:
    # A dry run for a DOI the registry already holds said WOULD ADD, though the run itself updates that entry.
    import add_reference
    from refs import registry

    held = _entry(key="held1995title", doi="10.1/held", url=None, isbn=[], verified_by="crossref")
    saved: list[object] = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(add_reference, "CACHE_DIR", tmp_path)
    monkeypatch.setattr(add_reference, "by_doi", lambda cand, doi: (work(doi=doi), {}, ""))
    monkeypatch.setattr(registry, "load", lambda: [dict(held, source_strings=[])])
    monkeypatch.setattr(registry, "save", saved.append)
    source = ["--source", "Smith (1995), Journal of Finance 50(1)", "--used-by", unit]
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.argv", ["add_reference.py", *argv, *source])
    assert add_reference.main() == 0
    lines = capsys.readouterr().out.splitlines()
    assert len(lines) == 1 and lines[0].startswith(expected)
    assert len(saved) == writes
    if writes:
        # The run stores the union in the entry it saves, not only in its printed line.
        assert saved[0][0]["used_by"] == ["M2", "S7"]  # type: ignore[index]
